GUARD LANDED — Gerrit 1503 (`839477cd72`), LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, submitted and merged to origin/main.

CONCURRENCY NOTE, and it is the same pattern this ticket keeps hitting: while 1503 was in review another agent independently fixed defect 1 and landed it as `36a67ba662` ("24f7: fix dependency-audit close broken by rename"). Their fix was substantively identical to mine — same one-line `--force=<reason>` change, and even the same test strategy of feeding the emitted argv to the real `_parse_flags` rather than string-matching the flag. On rebase I dropped my duplicates rather than carry redundant coverage, so 1503 landed as the tree-wide guard ONLY. That is the part nobody else had, and the part that stops this from recurring a third time.

So the two defects landed as two commits:
- `36a67ba662` — the stale call site in `scripts/dependency_audit.py` (concurrent agent);
- `839477cd72` — the tree-wide guard test (this change).

The guard is now the thing that would have caught `36a67ba662`'s subject matter the moment 0767c38ebb landed, without anyone remembering to re-run a manual grep.

Verified on the landed tree: `tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py` + `tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py` = 76 passed. Full local suite green pre-rebase (11248 passed / 148 skipped; the single reported error was an artifact of my own commit moving HEAD mid-run — the test passes on a stable HEAD). CI green on all four matrices (ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13, macos 3.13) plus lint+typecheck, pip-audit, packaging and identity gates.

One CI hiccup worth recording: patch set 1's run was CANCELLED by a shared concurrency group when another change dispatched the same workflow on main — not a test failure. A `recheck` comment retriggered it and it passed clean.
